summary: No single open table holds jump height against body size across similarly built animals from insects to large mammals; the best repository data are a CC0 Zenodo table of per-individual take-off velocity, acceleration and muscle/body-mass ratio for 68 frog species (340 individuals), plus single-taxon sets (kangaroo rats, jumping spider, crickets, leafhoppers); AnimalTraits supplies body mass only and has no locomotor columns.
next_step: Use the anuran table (take-off velocity vs body mass within one clade and jumping mode) for a first pre-registered test of size-independence of take-off velocity, and compile the cross-taxon jump-height literature (fleas, locusts, galagos, kangaroos, humans) into a supplementary table with mechanism flags.
obstacles_confirmed: Jump height against size, from small jumpers to large mammals, is scattered through papers rather than held in one public dataset.
Elastic tendons and crouched postures violate the similar-construction premise and change the expected scaling.
